newsitem.title: PERU: Fujimori says hopes to leave Peru solid in 2000.
newsitem.headline: Fujimori says hopes to leave Peru solid in 2000.

text.p: A beleaguered President Alberto Fujimori said on Sunday he hoped to finish his second term in office in 2000 leaving Peru strong and with potential for the future.

"My commitment is to take Peru forward and leave the country solid, strong, viable and with enormous possibilities for everyone in the year 2000," Fujimori told a crowd of several thousand gathered at his residence to celebrate his 59th birthday.
Presidential elections are due in 2000, but Peruvians are divided on whether Fujimori is eligible to stand because of ambiguities in the country's constitution.

Fujimori, who has been in office since 1990, has not said if he will try to run for an unprecedented third term. But opposition congressmen have called for the president to use his State of the Nation address on Monday to make clear he will not stand in 2000.

Fujimori, who was returned to office in 1995 with an overwhelming 64 percent of the vote, is facing his worst political crisis in seven years after plummeting dramatically in the polls in recent months.
Fewer than one in five Peruvians approve of his government.

The president's decline in popularity began in May when his supporters in congress ousted three Constitutional Court judges whose independent legal rulings had blocked the way for Fujimori to stand in the 2000 elections.
Fujimori's popularity continued to slide due to a slew of recent scandals involving alleged abuses of power by the security forces.
The crisis deepened last week when opposition media cast doubt on his right to rule, claiming he may have been born in Japan and not Peru as required by the constitution.
